text: Determine the exact current authority, trigger, wording, and practical obligation of every directive G0-G24, including overlaps and explicit or implicit precedence relationships.

source.user_intent: The directives must be accurate, practical, grounded, useful, and not cause contradictions or bloat.

acceptance_intent: Every current directive is decomposed into its protected intent, mandatory actions, prohibited actions, activation condition, and stop condition; no G-rule is omitted.

planner_obligations.description: Carry the complete G0-G24 intent and obligation inventory into the replacement mapping.

text: Determine the exact distribution and consumption topology for directives across canonical source, generated projections, installed skills, hooks, corpus synchronization, and repository-local instruction surfaces.

source.user_intent: A corrected directive contract must reach the places that actually govern Codex and related workflows.

acceptance_intent: Every authoritative writer, generated consumer, installed copy, validation test, and external approval boundary is named without treating generated files as independent authority.

planner_obligations.description: Plan promotion and validation across every grounded directive consumer without directly editing generated authority.

text: Determine which parts of the observed prevention-task loop were caused by directive or playbook contracts, which were caused by tooling defects, and which were caused by the agent failing to enforce existing scope rules.

source.user_intent: Do not use the directives as an excuse for agent inability.

acceptance_intent: The cause chain separately identifies rule defects, procedural amplification, tool defects, and agent non-compliance, with no monocausal or self-exculpatory conclusion.

planner_obligations.description: Preserve the evidence-backed causality distinction so the redesign fixes contracts without masking agent accountability.

text: Define one explicit authority hierarchy in which higher-priority safety and user authorization constrain lower-level directives, while playbooks, skills, sequences, blockers, and diagnostics can restrict or stop work but cannot create new scope.

source.user_intent: The directive system must not cause contradictions or expand work under the surface.

acceptance_intent: For every conflict class, one authority wins deterministically and no lower layer can authorize files, repositories, outcomes, external effects, or remediation excluded by the task envelope.

planner_obligations.description: Plan the canonical precedence and non-expansion contract and its validation tests.

text: Define a compact frozen task authorization envelope containing the practical outcome, acceptance evidence, allowed change and evidence surfaces, authorized enabling work, exclusions, external-effect permissions, and stop conditions.

source.user_intent: Practical subgoals must be completed without silently changing the completion plan.

acceptance_intent: A fresh executor can decide whether a discovered action is authorized using the envelope alone; ambiguity produces one question or a stop, never inferred scope.

planner_obligations.description: Plan the minimal task-envelope schema, freeze point, change gate, and human-readable presentation.

text: Define context-sensitive handling for product defects, explicitly authorized enabling-tool defects, out-of-scope infrastructure failures, harmless invocation mistakes, consequential anomalies, and unavailable evidence.

source.user_intent: The system must neither bypass real controls nor turn every support failure into another implementation project.

acceptance_intent: Each failure class has objective classification evidence and exactly one permitted response: correct within scope, retry an unchanged invocation, diagnose and stop, or request a bounded decision.

planner_obligations.description: Plan the failure-classification decision table and non-recursive recovery boundary.

text: Separate universal behavioral directives from task-envelope fields, playbook methods, operational sequence commands, tool schemas, and incident-specific examples while retaining traceability between layers.

source.user_intent: Directives should make sense generally rather than be shaped around the current task.

acceptance_intent: Every retained obligation exists at one correct authority layer; cross-layer references do not duplicate commands or create circular mandates.

planner_obligations.description: Plan relocation of procedural content and traceable references without losing enforcement intent.

text: Produce a complete disposition and replacement mapping for every current directive G0-G24: retain, revise, merge, move, or retire, with rationale, preserved intent, activation condition, authorized action, prohibition, and stop condition.

source.user_intent: Re-specify each G directive without skimming any needed effort.

acceptance_intent: All 25 current directives appear exactly once in the mapping; no protected intent disappears and no replacement contains an unconditional subprocess that can expand scope.

planner_obligations.description: Plan the exact canonical rewrite using the complete disposition and replacement map.

text: Define a representative scenario suite that proves the directive system produces one practical authorized action or one explicit stop condition without contradiction, unsafe bypass, recursive remediation, or hidden scope growth.

source.user_intent: The replacement must be proven generally useful, not merely described differently.

acceptance_intent: The suite covers local fixes, features, research, review, remote operations, migrations, broken test tooling, broken governance tooling, anomalies, long workflows, dirty trees, and out-of-scope root causes with expected behavior and forbidden behavior.

planner_obligations.description: Plan executable or deterministic contract tests for every grounded representative scenario.

text: Keep the directive system human-graspable: concise enough to apply during work, explicit enough to audit, and free of duplicated ceremony, hidden state, unexplained identifiers, or mandatory process that obscures the practical result.

source.user_intent: The directives must be practical and useful rather than abstract descriptions hiding unproductive work.

acceptance_intent: A user can see the current outcome, boundary, progress, decision, and stop reason without reading implementation machinery; routine work does not require a full rule audit.

planner_obligations.description: Plan concise directive structure, presentation rules, and usability checks without weakening auditability.

text: Preserve or strengthen safety, evidence quality, schema accuracy, destructive-action protection, external-effect approval, dirty-tree preservation, honest reporting, and complete-fix quality while removing process bloat.

source.user_intent: The correction must be generally better, not a task-specific weakening of safeguards.

acceptance_intent: No scenario gains authority to commit, push, deploy, access secrets, alter external state, guess schemas, overwrite user changes, or claim unproven completion; complete fixes remain required inside authorized scope.

planner_obligations.description: Plan explicit non-regression tests for safety, approval, evidence, preservation, and completion claims.

text: Define a bounded adoption, projection, validation, and rollback contract for replacing the canonical directives and synchronizing every authoritative consumer without directly editing generated surfaces or silently changing unrelated playbooks.

source.user_intent: The corrected directives must become the real governing behavior reliably and safely.

acceptance_intent: The canonical edit surface, generated projections, installed copies, corpus boundary, validation commands, approval gates, and rollback condition are named and finite before implementation begins.

planner_obligations.description: Plan the canonical edit, projection refresh, installed-skill alignment, corpus synchronization decision, validation, and rollback sequence.
